setup:
Assumptions (stated, not verified): the service is a Python stdlib HTTP service; the SQLite file path is configurable; the test suite lives under tests/. No command below was run by me — each is quoted from the plan or development outline and must be executed by the reader.

1. Use a Python 3 environment with only the standard library plus the test runner already present in the offline container.
2. Start the service against a chosen SQLite file (path is an implementer choice per requirements assumptions). The plan's T-1 requires the schema to be created idempotently on first start and to tolerate a second start on the same file.
3. Run the suite offline: `python -m pytest tests -q` or `python -m unittest discover -s tests` (from the development outline verification notes).
4. Restart check: create a link, stop the service, start again on the same SQLite file, follow the code, expect 302 with the original Location (plan T-7, outline verification notes).

No outbound network access is required or used (S-4-1).
usage:
Create: send a POST to /links with the long URL as a form field or JSON body (shape is an implementer choice per requirements assumptions). A valid absolute http/https URL returns 200 with a copyable short URL, either absolute (built from the request host) or a path containing the code — the form is an implementer choice. Missing, empty, non-absolute, or non-http(s) values return 400 and create no link.

Follow: send a GET to /{code} with a 7-character base62 code. A known code returns 302 with Location equal to the stored long URL. An unknown code returns 404 with no redirect. Links do not expire and have no click limit; no click or usage data is written or read on the follow path.

Error bodies have no required format; only status codes are asserted (requirements assumptions, plan assumptions).
architecture:
From the design: five components. The HTTP handler layer routes POST /links and GET /{code} and maps outcomes to 400/404/302. The URL validator is a pure function accepting only absolute http/https URLs, with no network calls. The code generator produces 7-character base62 codes and retries on collision. The link store is SQLite, holding code->long_url with a UNIQUE constraint on code, created idempotently at startup and reused across restarts. The response builder returns the short URL in copyable form and sets the Location header on redirect.

Data flow, create: client POST /links -> handler parses body -> validator checks absolute http/https -> generator produces a 7-char base62 code -> store insert under UNIQUE(code); on collision, regenerate and retry -> response builder returns the short URL. Data flow, follow: client GET /{code} -> handler -> store lookup -> 302 with Location=long_url if found, 404 if not; no click data written or read.

Key design decisions: D-1, the SQLite UNIQUE constraint is the single source of truth for collisions, so no application-level lock is needed. D-2, codes are random 7-char base62 with retry, so the same long URL submitted twice yields two distinct short URLs. D-3, validation uses stdlib parsing only, requiring scheme in {http, https} and an absolute form, with no DNS or reachability check. D-4, the follow path is lookup plus 302 only. D-5, the schema is created idempotently at startup. Rejected alternatives: in-memory dict (fails restart persistence), counter codes (predictable), hash-derived codes (same URL would map to the same code, conflicting with S-1-2), and any external framework or database (violates the stdlib+SQLite offline constraint).

How it was built, from the plan: T-1 project skeleton and SQLite schema bootstrap; T-2 URL validator; T-3 code generator with collision retry; T-4 LinkStore insert and lookup (depends on T-1); T-5 POST /links create endpoint (depends on T-2, T-3, T-4); T-6 GET /{code} follow endpoint (depends on T-4); T-7 end-to-end offline and persistence test suite (depends on T-5, T-6).

Development work, from the outline: changes were made in app.py and link_store.py. The handler had used HTTP/1.0 (the BaseHTTPRequestHandler default), so the server closed the connection after each response and urllib hit 'Remote end closed connection without response'. Setting protocol_version to HTTP/1.1 with an explicit Content-Length on every response keeps the connection alive so clients can read the status line and headers. The store connection is opened with check_same_thread=False because ThreadingHTTPServer serves each request on a new thread while sharing one sqlite3 connection; without it, concurrent requests raise ProgrammingError and the connection is dropped mid-response. The outline states no other behaviour changed: validation, code generation, redirect, and 404 semantics are untouched.
examples: Create (shape is an implementer choice; not run by me): POST /links with the long URL as a form field or JSON body. Expected on success: 200 with a copyable short URL, absolute or path form.
Create, invalid input: POST /links with a missing, empty, non-absolute, or non-http(s) value. Expected: 400 and no new row in the store.
Create, same URL twice: two successful submissions of the same long URL. Expected: two distinct short URLs, each redirecting to that long URL (S-1-2).
Follow, known code: GET /{code}. Expected: 302 with Location equal to the stored long URL (S-2-1).
Follow, unknown code: GET /{code} for a code that was never stored. Expected: 404 with no Location header (S-2-2).
Restart persistence: create a link, stop the service, start again on the same SQLite file, follow the code. Expected: 302 with the original Location (S-3-3, S-4-3).

Offline suite: `python -m pytest tests -q` or `python -m unittest discover -s tests`. Expected per the outline: previously failing HTTP tests now receive a status line and headers instead of RemoteDisconnected. I did not run this.
knownLimits: No authentication, API keys, rate limiting, or abuse protection (requirements assumptions).
No custom aliases, expiry, click limits, click tracking, statistics, or listing endpoint (requirements assumptions).
Only http and https targets are accepted; other schemes are rejected.
Error responses use plain HTTP status codes with no required body format.
Open redirect / abuse risk: any http(s) target is accepted, so the service can mask malicious links; out of scope for this version and flagged for a future requirement (design risks).
Code space is 62^7 (~3.5e12); collision rate should be monitored and code length revisited at scale (design risks).
Unbounded retry is a risk; the implementer sets a retry limit and returns 5xx on exhaustion (design risks, plan T-3).
SQLite write contention under concurrent creates is accepted for this version's scope (design risks).
An absolute short URL built from the Host header can be spoofed; a path-only short URL is an allowed alternative (design risks).
No rate limiting means trivial resource exhaustion; explicitly out of scope (design risks).
The exact request body shape, short URL form, base62 alphabet, retry limit, and SQLite file path are implementer choices and are not fixed by the supplied artifacts.
The development outline's verification notes are claims from that artifact; I did not run the suite, so the fix outcome is unverified here.
